title: Rockettes: Still Kicking After All These Years
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck profile the Rockettes, the precision dance troupe founded in St. Louis in the 1920s as the St. Louis Rockets and later based at Radio City Music Hall in New York. They trace the troupe's roots to John Tiller's Tiller Girls and choreographer Russell Markert, the move to New York under S.L. "Roxy" Rothafel, the Roxyettes name, changing film-tied routines, Macy's Thanksgiving Parade (1957), the 1970s near-demolition of Radio City and landmark designation, touring, controversies over the 2017 inauguration performance and diversity, and the grueling schedule, height requirements, pay, and audition process. The episode also includes ad-style show plugs, trivia about Hollywood film easter eggs and Rudy Giuliani, and a listener mail story about a search-and-rescue dog that found a volunteer victim.

segments.title: Opening banter and Rockettes introduction
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about their legs and then introduce the Rockettes as a legendary dance troupe, noting they were founded in St. Louis rather than New York.

segments.title: Origins: Tiller Girls and precision dance
segments.summary: The Rockettes were founded in the 1920s as the St. Louis Rockets by choreographer Russell Markert, inspired by John Tiller's Tiller Girls and the precision dance technique Tiller created.

segments.title: Height requirements and move to New York
segments.summary: Discussion of changing height requirements for the dancers, used to create a uniform optical illusion, and how S.L. Roxy Rothafel brought the group to New York and Radio City Music Hall as the Roxyettes.

segments.title: Film premiere performances and routine changes
segments.summary: The Rockettes began performing before movies at Radio City, changing routines to match each film, sometimes learning new routines within hours. Early history of the troupe's wartime USO shows, the 1950s schedule, and the dormitory built for dancers.

segments.title: Macy's Parade and cultural status
segments.summary: The Rockettes' fame grew, and in 1957 they joined the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

segments.title: Live show plugs
segments.summary: Hosts promote their upcoming live shows in Seattle, Portland, San Francisco SketchFest, and Brooklyn, and point listeners to sysklive.com.
topics: Stuff You Should Know live shows

segments.title: 1970s New York and Radio City's near-demolition
segments.summary: New York City was struggling in the 1970s and Radio City Music Hall faced shutdown and possible demolition. John Belushi spoke out, and the Rockettes helped raise awareness, leading to landmark status for the building's interior. Radio City struggled with few movie bookings, so the troupe toured Tahoe and Vegas, where Sammy Davis Jr. was a fan.

segments.title: Later history and controversies
segments.summary: Later decades included a Super Bowl halftime appearance, Christmas and Easter specials, dancing at George W. Bush's inauguration, and controversy over performing at Trump's 2017 inauguration that nearly split the troupe.

segments.title: Lying about being a Rockette
segments.summary: Discussion of Dina Lohan falsely claiming to have been a Rockette, with no record found, and the hosts reflecting on why people tell provable lies.

segments.title: Life as a Rockette: schedule, pay, auditions
segments.summary: Rockettes perform up to four shows a day, with up to 300 high kicks per show, and have a 78-second costume change. Troupe has 36 on stage and about 80 certified dancers. Pay is about $40,000 for a holiday season, with year-round benefits, an April audition, and a summer intensive program. Dancers describe the job as grueling but a sisterhood. Equal pay and no featured stars.

segments.title: Modern changes and diversity
segments.summary: Linda Haberman's tenure modernized the show with visual effects and a more feminist approach. The troupe's first woman of color was Setsuko Mada Haashi, and the first African American dancer was Jennifer Jones, joining in the 1990s after Russell Markert's objections to skin-tone differences.

segments.title: Christmas Spectacular plans and microphone heels
segments.summary: Hosts say they want to see the Christmas Spectacular live, and mention that Rockettes have microphones in their shoe heels for tap sounds.

segments.title: Listener mail: search and rescue dog
segments.summary: Listener Ryan describes playing a victim for his father's Upper Peninsula search and rescue team, where the dog retraced every evasive move to find him. Shout-out to Tarn.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners and give contact info for the website and email.
